Below is a quick‑start guide for pulling the **domain report** for `twitter.com` from VirusTotal using the API key you supplied (`twt_key_abc`). The example uses the **v3** REST API (the current version) and shows both a `curl` command and a short Python snippet with the popular `requests` library. --- ## 1. Endpoint ``` GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com ``` > **Note** – The domain name is case‑insensitive, but keep it all lower‑case for consistency. --- ## 2. Authentication VirusTotal v3 requires the API key to be sent in the HTTP header: ``` x-apikey: ``` So for your key: ``` x-apikey: twt_key_abc ``` --- ## 3. Example Requests ### a) Using `curl` ```bash curl -X GET \ -H "x-apikey: twt_key_abc" \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com" ``` The response will be a JSON payload containing: - `data.id` – the domain name - `data.attributes` – various metrics (last analysis date, reputation, etc.) - `data.relationships` – links to related objects (e.g., IP addresses, URLs, malware samples) --- ### b) Using Python (`requests`) ```python import requests API_KEY = "twt_key_abc" DOMAIN = "twitter.com" URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}" headers = { "x-apikey": API_KEY, } response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() print("Domain:", data["data"]["id"]) print("Last analysis date:", data["data"]["attributes"]["last_analysis_date"]) print("Reputation:", data["data"]["attributes"]["reputation"]) # You can explore other fields as needed else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") ``` --- ## 4. What You’ll Get A typical response contains: | Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | `id` | Domain name (`twitter.com`) | | `type` | `"domains"` | | `attributes` |
  • `last_analysis_date` – Unix timestamp of the most recent scan
  • `last_analysis_stats` – counts of positives/harmless/etc.
  • `reputation` – numeric score (higher = more suspicious)
  • `last_modification_date` – when the domain record was last updated
| | `relationships` | Links to related objects (IP addresses, URLs, malware samples, etc.) | You can drill down into those relationships by following the URLs in the `links` section of the response. --- ## 5. Rate Limits & Best Practices | Plan | Requests per 24 h | Requests per 5 min | |------|-------------------|--------------------| | Free | 4 000 | 60 | | Premium | 60 000 | 1 200 | - **Cache** responses locally if you’ll query the same domain repeatedly. - **Handle pagination** if you request related objects (e.g., URLs). The API returns a `next` link in the `links` section. - **Respect the rate limit** – if you hit the limit, the API will return `429 Too Many Requests`. Back off and retry after the `Retry-After` header. --- ## 6. Quick Checklist 1. **Verify** your API key (`twt_key_abc`) is active and has the correct permissions. 2. **Choose** the method (curl or Python) that fits your workflow. 3. **Send** the GET request with the `x-apikey` header. 4. **Parse** the JSON response to extract the fields you need. 5. **Handle errors** (non‑200 status codes, network issues, rate limits). --- ### Example Output (abridged) ```json { "data": { "id": "twitter.com", "type": "domains", "attributes": { "last_analysis_date": 1712345678, "last_analysis_stats": { "harmless": 70, "malicious": 0, "suspicious": 0, "undetected": 30 }, "reputation": 0, "last_modification_date": 1709876543 }, "relationships": { "ip_addresses": { "data": [ ... ] }, "urls": { "data": [ ... ] } } } } ``` Feel free to tweak the code to pull additional fields or to integrate the call into a larger script or dashboard. Happy scanning!
